content:
- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (especially when sentiment > 0.5) — model tends to overshoot and then correct.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is consistently low or negative (sentiment < 0.4) — model fails to capture downward pressure.
- Lag in price correction: model often delays reacting to recent price drops or sentiment shifts — adjust forecast to align with 1–2 prior days’ sentiment trends.
- Mean reversion bias: model overreacts to short-term volatility; reduce forecast amplitude for periods with high sentiment volatility.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts are overly optimistic in early cycles (e.g., 2024-11-18 to 2024-11-22) — reduce forecast peak values by 2–5% for early horizon.
- Sentiment-driven bias: when sentiment is high (0.8+), model overweights bullish momentum; when sentiment is low (0.2–0.4), model underweights bearish momentum — adjust forecast slope based on sentiment average over last 5 days.
